brief.headline: Debora fell at home on 2026-10-02 and now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing. Her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and has asked for respite.

items.statement: Debora fell in the kitchen on 2026-10-02 while reaching for a cabinet. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness and had a small left forearm skin tear. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The 10-02 nursing note matches every detail: the kitchen fall, no head strike or LOC, the left forearm skin tear, high fall risk and the PT referral.

items.statement: On 2026-10-05 PT found her gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and Timed Up and Go was 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: The PT note matches on gait, cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation, bathroom grab bars and twice-weekly visits.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found she needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, and she was independent at last review. On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting out of the tub, and she said she has been skipping showers for fear of slipping. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note and the aide note together support the moderate assistance, the prior independence, the tub help, the skipped showers, and the OT recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches on Kevin's exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings, the respite request, and the discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), with a recheck planned in 4 weeks. The pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The notes provided show no recheck or repeat PHQ-9. The fall on 2026-10-02 came about 3 weeks after the start.

items.statement: She is avoiding showers out of fear of slipping (2026-10-19), and depressive symptoms were being treated as of 2026-09-13. The notes provided do not show any follow-up on mood.
items.verifier_note: The aide note supports the avoided showers, and the PCP note supports the depressive symptoms being treated as of 09-13. No mood follow-up appears in the cited notes.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The last doses were on 2026-04-25 and 2025-04-19.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the prior IDT review date is known, so all changes are measured from the correct baseline.

Falls and injuries: any falls, near-falls, or fall-related injuries in the window, including circumstances and whether a fall risk assessment was done. Note that sertraline was started 2026-09-13 and metoprolol is ongoing, so check for dizziness or orthostatic symptoms.

ED visits and hospital admissions in the window: reason, discharge summary, and whether follow-up appointments or medication reconciliation occurred. Pay attention to ischemic heart disease and COPD-related exacerbations (chest pain, dyspnea, nitroglycerin use).

Cardiac symptoms and cardiac medication review: chest pain episodes, nitroglycerin spray use frequency, and adherence to clopidogrel, simvastatin, and metoprolol. Flag any missed doses or gaps in refills.

Respiratory status: COPD symptoms, rescue albuterol use frequency, fluticasone/salmeterol inhaler adherence and technique, oxygen needs if any, and recent respiratory infections or antibiotic/steroid courses.

Medication changes since last review: confirm the sertraline start on 2026-09-13 (PHQ-9 of 14) is documented with indication, prescriber, and planned follow-up. Check for early adverse effects (GI upset, sleep change, bleeding risk given concurrent clopidogrel, hyponatremia signs) and whether a repeat PHQ-9 is scheduled.

Mood and cognition: review PHQ-9 trajectory, suicidality screening, social withdrawal, sleep, appetite, and attendance at appointments. Check for any cognitive screen results and whether depressive symptoms are linked to chronic pain, breast cancer history, or recent cardiac events.

Pain management: chronic pain severity scores, current analgesic use (none listed on active medication list, so verify OTC or prescribed analgesics are not missing from reconciliation), and functional impact on daily activities.

Weight, BMI, and metabolic trend: obesity (BMI 30+) and prediabetes history. Review weight trend, most recent HbA1c or glucose, and lipid results relevant to simvastatin. Also review thyroid status for idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine (TSH timing and last result).

Function, caregiver, and care-plan items: ADL/IADL changes, transportation and social support, caregiver situation, blood pressure and heart rate trends, and any care-plan goals or assessments that came due in the window (e.g., annual reassessment, breast cancer surveillance status, vaccinations) and whether they were completed.
